Across the network, members develop reputations based on their patterns of contribution. Those who consistently engage in cooperative exchange tend to be recognized as reliable participants whose involvement others value when considering future collaborations and ongoing partnerships. The community's sense of who belongs at its center is shaped by these observed patterns of reciprocity.

Observations of similar networks indicate that cooperative relationships established early tend to be more durable and mutually beneficial over time. Members who invest in mutual engagement from the beginning often find their standing strengthens as the network matures. The structure of these networks tends to reward early and consistent cooperation.
